samples.summary: None of the text-editor plumbing that actually produces the affinity is tested (click, shift+click, drag, shift+Home, shift+arrow)
samples.evidence: The user-visible fix is that a click/drag/caret-move on a wrap boundary tags the selection endpoint with `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts ~1517 mousedown, ~1770 header/footer drag, ~1792 body drag, ~2772 shift+arrow, ~2805 shift+Home). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-constructs DocPositions and calls `computeSelectionRects` directly — it never goes through TextEditor, so it cannot fail if the editor forgets to attach the affinity, attaches the wrong one (e.g. the shift+Home hardcoded 'forward' at offset 0, or shift+Up/Down using the cursor's stale affinity), or drops it on `setRange`. I grepped packages/docs/test for `lineAffinity` (only the new file and hf-caret-selection.test.ts, which tests computeHFCursorPixel), and for `Home|getVisualLineStart|updateDragSelection|mousedown|mousemove` (only cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts and image-selection-overlay.test.ts, neither of which touches selection affinity). Result: the entire producer side ships with zero coverage while the rect consumer is well covered.

samples.summary: lineAffinity round-trip through Yorkie anchoring/presence has no test, in a package with no tsc either
samples.evidence: The diff threads `lineAffinity` through `anchorDocPosition`, `anchorDocRange`, `clampPosToModel`, `resolveAnchoredDocPosition`, `fallbackAnchoredDocPosition` and `updateCursorPos`, and changes `anchorDocPosition`'s default from `'backward'` to `undefined` (affecting `setCompositionStart` and everything that resolves an anchor back). I grepped packages/frontend/tests for `lineAffinity`/`affinity` — no matches — and the existing `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor` tests in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts (lines ~1836-2026) assert only blockId/offset. So nothing verifies the affinity survives anchor→resolve, nor that dropping it for composition anchors is intentional. packages/frontend has no `tsc --noEmit` lane, so even a type-level slip here is uncaught.

samples.summary: The cell-internal affinity path (resolvePositionPixel + lineIdxForOffset) is changed but untested
samples.evidence: buildRects' cell-internal branch (selection.ts:267-366) now feeds the endpoint-derived affinity into `resolvePositionPixel` and `lineIdxForOffset` instead of hardcoded 'forward'/'backward'. The new test fixture sets `blockParentMap: new Map()` (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:53), so every test takes the non-cell branch; `computeSelectionRects` is called from no other test file. An explicit 'backward' start or 'forward' end inside a wrapped table cell — the only case where this branch's behavior actually changed — is never exercised.

samples.summary: Two of the six tests are non-discriminating (they pass identically under the pre-change behavior)
samples.evidence: Test 'keeps the affinity when the range is reversed' (line 127) sets `lineAffinity: 'forward'` on the focus, but the resulting start would also read forward under the new no-affinity default (line 260, `?? 'forward'`), so it does not actually prove normalizeRange preserved the field — an implementation that stripped `lineAffinity` during normalization would still pass. Likewise 'keeps a backward-affinity end' (line 138) matches the default end reading. Only the explicit-'backward'-start (line 104) and explicit-'forward'-end (line 149) cases can fail if the plumbing is removed. A reversed-range test with `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on the focus would be the discriminating version.

samples.summary: Loose assertions in the multi-line cases
samples.evidence: Lines 112-114 and 155-156 assert only `rects.length > 1` and a `y` value; the comment claims the first rect is a 'zero-width tail on line 0' but no test asserts `width === 0` or the x positions. The tests would still pass if the boundary rect had a bogus width, so the described shape is documented but not verified.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the affinity-producing sites in text-editor.ts (mousedown pos build at 1514-1525, drag focus at 1776 and 1798, shift+arrow focus at 2772-2780, shift+Home hardcoded 'forward' at 2803-2818) have no test anywhere. The single new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-builds layouts and calls computeSelectionRects directly with literal lineAffinity fields on anchor/focus — it never instantiates TextEditor, never goes through Selection.setRange/getNormalizedRange, and dispatches no events, so it passes regardless of what the editor attaches. Searched beyond the reviewer's greps: repo-wide `lineAffinity` hits only two test files (the other, hf-caret-selection.test.ts, calls computeHFCursorPixel/computeHFSelectionRects directly with an affinity argument); `mousedown|mousemove|pointerdown` in packages/docs/test yields only an unrelated comment in image-selection-overlay.test.ts; `getPositionFromMouse|updateDragSelection|extendSelection|handleMouseDown|paginatedPixelToPosition` has test hits only in sheets/worksheet-mouse.test.ts and docs/pagination.test.ts; `LineStart|LineEnd|moveVertical|selectTo` has zero hits in packages/docs/test; no e2e suite exists; none of the 182 frontend test files reference lineAffinity, so the yorkie-doc-store endpoint-affinity plumbing is untested too. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md steps 3-5) confirms only the rect-level test was planned. A real behavior change (which line a click/drag/caret-move tags) ships with no meaningful test on the producer side — major, in the missing-tests lane.

verdict.reason: The lineAffinity threading through the Yorkie anchoring/presence path in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (AnchoredDocPosition.lineAffinity l.67; anchorDocPosition l.916-939; clampPosToModel l.967; anchorDocRange l.994-999; resolveAnchoredDocPosition l.1054/1072; fallbackAnchoredDocPosition l.1124; setCompositionStart l.1204 passing no affinity; updateCursorPos l.2967-2994) has no test anywhere in the repo. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for "affinity" finds only two test files, both in packages/docs/test/view, and selection-line-affinity.test.ts imports computeSelectionRects from packages/docs/src/view/selection.js — it tests rect painting, not the store's anchor->resolve round trip. The frontend 'local caret anchoring' suite (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1828-2026) always calls updateCursorPos with only {blockId, offset} and asserts only {blockId, offset} via toEqual, which ignores undefined properties, so it passes whether or not affinity survives; the composition-anchor cases (2011-2026) likewise never assert affinity, leaving the 'backward' -> undefined default change unverified. The repo's own task file (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:49-53) names only the docs view test. The secondary tsc point also holds: packages/frontend/package.json has no typecheck script and scripts/verify-self.mjs typechecks every other package but not frontend. Missing test for a real behavior change = major in this lens.
